sourceIssues.description: The slide does not explicitly state the conservative-force/path-independence condition for U(r). Questions using the force integral state that condition instead of treating an arbitrary force as admitting a position potential.

The blanket statement that gyroscopic and non-potential forces cannot be handled is not established as a universal result by the displayed restricted energy formulation. Retain explicit slide attribution if examined; do not teach it as a general impossibility of all generalized-force formulations. The dL/partial q mixed numerator typography is clarified by consistent page437 notation.

The torque-only label for tau applies to all-revolute coordinates. The next page includes prismatic coordinates, and the RP final equations explicitly include a force; mixed-coordinate questions distinguish N·m and N.

The angle-arc arrow alone is not a sufficient sign convention. Questions state theta positive from +X toward downward +Y, consistent with the displayed gravitational potential −mgl sin(theta), and assume the torsional spring is undeflected at theta=0.
The final equality to zero silently specializes the preceding equation with applied torque tau to the unforced case. Generated questions state tau=0 explicitly or retain tau on the right.

The source writes sin(90−theta) without a degree mark while the spring coordinate normally uses radians. Use cos(theta), or write sin(pi/2−theta) for radians; numerical spring torque always uses theta in radians.

The RP figure does not identify a horizontal reference axis. State theta1 measured from horizontal toward positive upward height, consistent with its positive g(m1 l1+m2 d2)sin(theta1) potential. This differs from the single-DOF downward-positive convention.

In the lower standalone M_x display, the character between Izz2 and m2 d2² resembles an underscore rather than a plus. Earlier K, the upper scalar torque and the upper full matrix equation all have a clear plus. Derive M11 from the positive kinetic-energy coefficient and disclose the inconsistent lower typography.

V denotes potential energy in the first summary line but a velocity-dependent generalized-force vector in the dynamic decomposition. Questions distinguish scalar U (or V_potential) from vector V_velocity and do not conflate them.
